reason: Section 25 lets an employee complaining of a section 24 violation choose final and binding collective-agreement arbitration, if available, or file a written complaint with the Commission within one year, after which the Commission refers timely complaints to an appointed arbitrator.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Complaint path and time limit for discriminatory action
proposedGroups.reason: Section 25 lets an employee complaining of a section 24 violation choose final and binding collective-agreement arbitration, if available, or file a written complaint with the Commission within one year, after which the Commission refers timely complaints to an appointed arbitrator.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an employee brings a discriminatory-action complaint, the filing deadline, and the Commission referral duty.

reason: Section 26 has distinct topics for arbitrator powers and remedies, written findings and clarification, court review and record transmission, and the definition of arbitrator.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Arbitrator powers, discriminatory-action findings, and remedial orders
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections give the arbitrator Industrial Relations Act powers, authorize remedial orders after discriminatory findings, and require written findings with reasons and orders to be provided to the parties and Commission.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the arbitrator powers, available remedies, and written finding requirements for discriminatory-action complaints.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Clarification requests and court review of arbitrator orders
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow a party to request clarification or omitted-matter treatment, permit court review for jurisdiction or legal error, require service and record delivery, and state possible court orders, effective-date orders and Rules of Court application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify how arbitrator orders may be clarified or reviewed by the Court of King Bench and what procedural rules apply.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Meaning of arbitrator in discriminatory-action proceedings
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 26(12) defines arbitrator for section 26 as the arbitrator appointed under subsection 25(2).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who counts as the arbitrator for section 26.

reason: Section 27 permits the employee or Commission to file an arbitrator order in the Court of King Bench after the review period expires if a bound party fails to comply, and makes the filed order enforceable as a court judgment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court filing and judgment enforcement of arbitrator orders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 27 permits the employee or Commission to file an arbitrator order in the Court of King Bench after the review period expires if a bound party fails to comply, and makes the filed order enforceable as a court judgment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an arbitrator order is filed and enforced as a judgment when a party does not comply.

reason: Section 28 separates officer entry, inspection, document and investigation powers from technical-expert assistance and evidentiary use of certified copies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer entry, inspection, sampling, document, inquiry, investigation, and preservation powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 28(1) authorizes officers to enter and inspect places of employment, conduct tests and examinations, require and copy records, remove materials for copying, sample products or equipment, make inquiries, investigate incidents and occupational disease, and order things left undisturbed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the inspection, document, sampling, inquiry, investigation and preservation powers of occupational health and safety officers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Technical expert assistance and evidentiary use of certified copies
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 28(2) and (3) allow technical experts to accompany officers and make certified copies admissible as prima facie proof of originals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how technical experts may assist officers and how certified copies are used as evidence.

reason: Section 29 requires an officer carrying out an inspection to be accompanied by employee and employer committee members or representatives of each group when no committee exists or members are unavailable.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employee and employer accompaniment during officer inspections
proposedGroups.reason: Section 29 requires an officer carrying out an inspection to be accompanied by employee and employer committee members or representatives of each group when no committee exists or members are unavailable.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must accompany an officer during an inspection.

reason: Section 30 requires an officer, on demand, to produce the identification card signed by the President and Chief Executive Officer of the Commission.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer production of identification card on demand
proposedGroups.reason: Section 30 requires an officer, on demand, to produce the identification card signed by the President and Chief Executive Officer of the Commission.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the identification-card production duty of occupational health and safety officers.

reason: Section 31 allows an officer to give oral or written orders to any person for matters regulated, controlled or required by the Act or regulations, set a completion time, and requires oral orders to be written before the officer leaves the place of employment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer oral and written orders for Act or regulation matters
proposedGroups.reason: Section 31 allows an officer to give oral or written orders to any person for matters regulated, controlled or required by the Act or regulations, set a completion time, and requires oral orders to be written before the officer leaves the place of employment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an officer may give orders, how timing may be specified, and when an oral order must be reduced to writing.

reason: Section 32 has one topic for orders addressing unsafe or unhealthy working conditions and service of those orders, and another for tool, equipment, machine or device non-compliance orders and warnings.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Written officer orders for unsafe or unhealthy working conditions
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize written orders to specified workplace parties to suspend work, control danger, protect health and safety, or ensure compliance, and set service methods.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may receive a written officer order for unsafe conditions, what measures may be ordered, and how the order is served.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer orders and warnings for non-compliant tools, equipment, machines, or devices
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require an officer who finds non-compliant equipment to prohibit use, permit use only on safety conditions, or secure compliance, and to give written orders and attach warnings when use is prohibited.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the officer options for non-compliant tools, equipment, machines or devices and the warning requirement when use is prohibited.

reason: Section 33 prohibits obstructing or delaying an officer, knowingly giving false information, failing to produce required certificates or documents, and preventing an employee from appearing before or being questioned by an officer.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibitions against obstructing officers, false information, non-production, and preventing questioning
proposedGroups.reason: Section 33 prohibits obstructing or delaying an officer, knowingly giving false information, failing to produce required certificates or documents, and preventing an employee from appearing before or being questioned by an officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conduct prohibited in relation to occupational health and safety officers and their inquiries.

reason: Section 33.1 allows an officer who makes an order to require an employer written compliance report within the officer time period, signed by the employer and committee member or health and safety representative.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employer compliance report after officer order
proposedGroups.reason: Section 33.1 allows an officer who makes an order to require an employer written compliance report within the officer time period, signed by the employer and committee member or health and safety representative.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an employer compliance report may be required after an officer order and who signs it.

reason: The target is repeal-only text and contains no current operative study content.

Section 35 requires an officer who made a section 32 order to provide a copy to the committee or health and safety representative where one exists and permits posting; where neither exists, posting is mandatory.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Providing or posting copies of section 32 officer orders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 35 requires an officer who made a section 32 order to provide a copy to the committee or health and safety representative where one exists and permits posting; where neither exists, posting is mandatory.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when copies of section 32 orders are provided to committees or representatives and when posting is required.

reason: Section 36 prohibits removing a posted copy of a section 32 order without officer authorization and prohibits use of a place of employment or part where the officer has prohibited use except as permitted by the officer.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Restrictions after an officer order is posted
proposedGroups.reason: Section 36 prohibits removing a posted copy of a section 32 order without officer authorization and prohibits use of a place of employment or part where the officer has prohibited use except as permitted by the officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what may not be done after a section 32 officer order has been posted.

reason: Section 36.1 permits an officer who makes a written order under section 31 or 32 to impose an administrative penalty for a contravention specified in the order, within 14 days unless the Commission extends the period.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Administrative penalty authority after written officer orders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 36.1 permits an officer who makes a written order under section 31 or 32 to impose an administrative penalty for a contravention specified in the order, within 14 days unless the Commission extends the period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an officer may impose an administrative penalty and the time limit for doing so.

reason: Section 36.2 prevents both an administrative penalty and an offence charge for the same contravention, whether the penalty or the charge comes first.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mutual exclusion between administrative penalties and offence charges
proposedGroups.reason: Section 36.2 prevents both an administrative penalty and an offence charge for the same contravention, whether the penalty or the charge comes first.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 36.2 prevents duplicate administrative penalty and offence proceedings for the same contravention.

reason: Section 36.3 sets different administrative penalty ranges by role and then states how prior contraventions and continuing contraventions affect the amount.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Administrative penalty amounts by workplace role and repeat contravention
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set escalating maximum penalty amounts for employers and similar duty holders, supervisors or owners, and employees.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the maximum administrative penalty amounts for employers and similar parties, supervisors or owners, and employees for first and repeat contraventions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Three-year reset and continuing contravention multiplier for administrative penalties
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections deem a contravention first after three years since a prior notice and multiply the penalty by the number of days a contravention continues.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify how the three-year first-contravention reset and continuing-day multiplier affect administrative penalty amounts.

reason: Section 36.4 requires an officer to impose an administrative penalty by notice containing specified identity, contravention, amount, payment and appeal information, bars notices more than one year after first knowledge, and requires service within 14 days by personal service or registered mail.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice contents, one-year limit, and service of administrative penalties
proposedGroups.reason: Section 36.4 requires an officer to impose an administrative penalty by notice containing specified identity, contravention, amount, payment and appeal information, bars notices more than one year after first knowledge, and requires service within 14 days by personal service or registered mail.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an administrative penalty notice must contain, when it is time-barred, and how it must be served.

reason: Section 36.5 requires payment within 30 days after service, or within 30 days after the Chief Compliance Officer confirms or varies the amount on appeal, and makes the penalty payable to the Commission as part of the Accident Fund.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Payment deadline and Accident Fund destination for administrative penalties
proposedGroups.reason: Section 36.5 requires payment within 30 days after service, or within 30 days after the Chief Compliance Officer confirms or varies the amount on appeal, and makes the penalty payable to the Commission as part of the Accident Fund.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an administrative penalty must be paid and where the money goes.
